3c2d9cdd1a8c049fb9c7f4d9665f57eaf2a23f6d.summary: UK government statement (published 19 July 2021) attributing a Microsoft Exchange Server compromise, affecting over a quarter of a million servers, to Chinese state-backed actors. It attributes APT40 and APT31 to the Chinese Ministry of State Security and cites an NCSC assessment linking HAFNIUM to the Chinese state. Reported targets include maritime industries, naval defence contractors, government and Cambodian electoral entities. NCSC issued advice to over 70 affected organisations, and the UK calls on China to end the activity.

3cc32494460630c192e446f0d71371e1844fa964.summary: Group-IB blog on MuddyWater, described as an Iranian-government-linked group active in the Middle East since 2017. In 2019 it ran phishing against ASELSAN A.Ş, a Turkish defence electronics maker, using a PowerShell backdoor called POWERSTATS, with decoy documents including an F-35 specifications file. Of 34 ASELSAN email addresses in one decoy, 28 had appeared in earlier public leaks. The report also explores a possible link between MuddyWater and researcher Nima Nikjoo, which it calls unresolved, and describes leaks of Iranian APT group data on Telegram and the dark web.

3c6c22aab55b909387363ed473b352a0d699d2b9.summary: Symantec researchers describe Odinaff, a previously undocumented banking Trojan active since January of the article year. It targets banking, securities, trading, payroll and support-service organisations, mainly through malicious macro documents and password-protected archives. It spies on networks, steals credentials, and installs a second in-memory malware family called Batel. Researchers suspect a link to the Carbanak group. US banks are the most targeted, followed by Hong Kong, Australia and the UK.
